title: The Savoy Male and Female College
text:
about 1855. W. I. Hunt was born May 9, 1861, near the present town of Whitewright and attended rural schools in that locality. He had just reached man's estate when he entered the College in 1882. He was first in the Preparatory Department a year before entering on the stringent course for the A.B. degree. The Victorian Literary Society attracted him to membership, and he became a leader in student affairs, serving as editor of the Philomean Messenger during his last year in College. He was Julia S. Fielder, Miss John Mayer, of Eastland, Texas, was also a popular student at the College during this period, and teacher in that college.

Upon his graduation with the A.B. degree in the spring of 1887, he was invited to join the teaching staff and became a stockholder in the institution, for Professor Holland was seeking to strengthen his faculty at this time as there was need for an instructor in Greek. After teaching one year at higher math and Greek in the College, in the fall of 1888, Mr. Hunt shifted his teaching field to Trenton, Texas, where he was principal of the academy for one year. It was there that he had met and wooed Miss Mollie Lee, whose family lived on a farm near by, and they were duly married on August 9, 1888, at the beginning of his period of teaching.

In 1890 Mr. Hunt moved his family, which now included two children, to Stephenville, Texas, where he made many friends readily, and found public office an attractive career. In the more than forty years spent in Stephenville, he served variously as County Surveyor, County Clerk, District Clerk, and County Commissioner. He was also at one time City County Surveyor and a civil engineer.

When Mr. and Mrs. Hunt celebrated their golden wedding anniversary on August 9, 1938, they were surrounded by their four children and six of their twenty-six living grandons. Their children, who all live in Breckenridge, are Homer Hunt, who is a dentist; Mrs. Lessie Maddux; Mrs. Della Pitcher, whose husband is a salesman; Mrs. Ina Boomquist, a teacher in the city school; and Mrs. Eula Lockett, whose husband is an electrician.
